candidates.title: Evaluated program can set its own recorded score through the in-band metrics marker
candidates.description: The shared harness reads the score from the last line of the child's combined stdout and stderr that starts with the fixed marker '@@METRICS@@'. For 15 of the 21 problems the evaluator imports the LLM-generated program into the same interpreter that later prints that marker. Program code can therefore print its own marker line and end the interpreter (os._exit, or sys.exit, which the evaluators' 'except Exception' does not catch) before the genuine line is printed, or replace the evaluator's functions in memory. evaluation.py never checks the child's exit status, uses no per-run secret, and accepts any numeric non-NaN score, including values far above what the evaluator can produce. The forged value is returned to the framework as the fitness and is appended to EVAL_LOG by the trusted parent, which the file header describes as the place all frameworks' scores are read from. The lower-trust principal is the LLM output; the affected resource is the integrity of the benchmark scores and of the selection signal inside each run. The strongest control visible in source is the child process boundary with a 60 s limit, which does not separate the program from the marker's author. For the six evaluators that run the program in a further child process, the same marker channel might be reachable by a same-uid descendant that reopens the parent's stdout pipe through /proc and then stops the parent; that variant depends on operating-system behaviour and is not established from source.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The metrics channel is unauthenticated and shared with the untrusted program: run_evaluator.py executes the program inside the process that emits the marker, and evaluation.py trusts the last marker line without checking the exit status, a per-run secret or a plausible score range.

candidates.title: Evaluated program receives the path of the shared score log and can write records to it directly
candidates.description: EVAL_LOG is documented as the file from which every framework's scores are read. evaluation.py starts the evaluator child with the complete parent environment, so the log path exported by run_baseline.sh reaches run_evaluator.py, and the per-case children of the scientific problems and the circle_packing_26 wrapper inherit it again because they are started without an env argument. The log is an ordinary file owned by the uid that runs the program and is opened in append mode by the parent; nothing authenticates a record or restricts who appends, truncates or rewrites it. The lower-trust principal is the LLM output; the affected resource is the integrity of the score record that the cross-framework comparison relies on.

candidates.title: Processes started by an evaluated program outlive the evaluation and its time limit
candidates.description: evaluation.py starts the evaluator in a new session and states that this lets a timeout kill everything the child started. The group kill is sent only when communicate() times out, and only to the original process group. A descendant that the program moved to another session or group is not signalled, and when the evaluation finishes normally nothing is signalled at all, so a background process that does not hold the stdout pipe keeps running with the operator's uid and environment after the score has been recorded. The per-case runner of the scientific problems has the same structure, and the circle_packing_26 evaluator kills only its direct child. Because the evaluator child is in its own session, the group SIGTERM that run_baseline.sh relies on at the end of the budget does not reach in-flight evaluations, whose only supervisor is the adapter process being terminated. The task statements promise a hard 60 s limit on one core. A surviving process is not bound by it: it can continue computing and leave results for later programs of the same lineage, act on the score log after the parent has written the genuine record, and keep running after the framework run ends. The lower-trust principal is the LLM output; the affected resources are the compute-budget rule the comparison depends on and the operator's host after the run. A related robustness effect is that the communicate() call after the kill has no timeout, so a surviving descendant that still holds the pipe keeps evaluate() from returning.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Process lifetime is bound to the evaluation only through a process-group SIGKILL issued in the timeout handler; there is no kill on normal completion and no containment (subreaper, cgroup or PID namespace) for descendants that leave the group.

candidates.title: Scientific-problem programs can read the reference answers they are scored against
candidates.description: scientific_cases.py states that the program's entry function runs in a child process that receives only the case inputs and never the reference answer. That is true of the arguments, but the child runs under the same uid with no file-system restriction. For convection_diffusion_2d and helmholtz_2d the answers are stored in reference.npz beside the evaluator, world-readable and keyed by case name; for burgers_1d, nonnormal_eigenvalues and sparse_linear_systems the evaluator source regenerates the references from a fixed seed, so importing that file yields them. The absolute problem directory appears in the command line of the child's parent process, and BENCHMARK_PROBLEM is in the inherited environment. A program that returns the stored reference for the case it is given has relative error 0 and receives full marks on every case without solving the problem. The lower-trust principal is the LLM output; the affected resource is the validity of the scores of the five scientific-computing problems. The control named in source is the separate child process with input-only arguments.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Reference answers are kept in files readable by the process that runs the untrusted program, and the isolation claimed for that process covers only its arguments, not its file access or environment.

candidates.title: circle_packing_26 evaluator unpickles a results file controlled by the evaluated program
candidates.description: The circle_packing_26 evaluator is the one evaluator that runs the program in a child process of its own. The child returns its result by pickling the objects that run_packing() returned into a file next to the wrapper script, and the evaluator loads that file with pickle.load after checking only that the child exited with code 0. The objects are chosen by the program, and the program can also write the file itself because its path is the wrapper script path plus '.results'. Unpickling therefore executes program-chosen callables inside the run_evaluator.py process, which is the process that prints the metrics marker. That removes the only separation this evaluator has between the program and the scorer: code running there can emit its own metrics and end the process, and a SystemExit raised during the load is not caught by the evaluator's 'except Exception', while the child's stdout, whose lines after the first are reprinted without a prefix, has already been written. The lower-trust principal is the LLM output; the crossed boundary is child process to evaluator process; the affected resource is the integrity of this problem's scores. Both processes run under the same uid, so no additional operating-system privilege is claimed.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: run_with_timeout uses pickle as the result format for data produced by the untrusted child and loads it in the evaluator process with no restriction on the types that may be constructed.

candidates.title: Evaluation runs Python with the shared temp directory first on the module search path
candidates.description: The circle_packing_26 evaluator writes its wrapper script directly into the system temp directory and runs it as a script. Python then puts the script's directory, normally the world-writable /tmp, at the front of the module search path, ahead of the standard library and site-packages, and the wrapper imports numpy, pickle and traceback. A file such as numpy.py or pickle.py present in that directory is imported and executed with the operator's uid on every circle_packing_26 evaluation, under any framework. The harness sets PYTHONNOUSERSITE but not safe-path mode. The results file is a predictable sibling name in the same directory, is opened by the child without exclusive creation, and is unpickled by the evaluator whenever it exists and the child exited with 0, so on hosts without the protected-file sysctls a file placed there by another account can be loaded. The same pattern reaches the 15 in-process evaluators when OpenEvolve is the framework: OpenEvolve writes each program directly into the temp directory and the evaluators insert the program's directory at sys.path[0] before importing it, so the program's own imports of modules not yet loaded, for example jax in the shipped initial programs, resolve from the shared directory first. Two lower-trust principals are affected differently. Another local account on a shared host could plant such a file and gain code execution as the operator; whether such accounts and a shared /tmp exist is a deployment fact. An evaluated program can plant one and thereby persist into every later evaluation and run on the host. The affected resources are the operator's account and the integrity of later evaluations.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Scripts and result files are created directly in the shared temp directory instead of a private directory, and the interpreters are started without isolated or safe-path mode, so the shared directory becomes an import location.

Single observable: <scratch>/t/marker is created, showing that a file in the temp directory was imported in place of the standard-library module during a normal evaluation. The evaluation then reports score 0 because the stand-in module is empty.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check on an evaluation host: run 'ls -ld "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"' and 'getent passwd' to see whether the temp directory is world-writable and shared with other accounts, and 'sysctl fs.protected_regular fs.protected_symlinks'.

hardening: benchmarks/problems/circle_packing_26/evaluator.py:105-139 interpolates program_path and temp_file.name unquoted into generated Python source (inside quotes and inside an f-string). No lower-trust value reaches these today, but an operator path containing a quote, backslash or brace breaks or changes the wrapper; pass the paths through sys.argv or repr().

benchmarks/problems/circle_packing_26/evaluator.py:208-210 uses a 600 s inner limit under a 60 s outer limit, so its timeout branch is unreachable in the shared harness, and the outer SIGKILL skips the finally block (184-189): the wrapper script and results file stay in the temp directory after every timed-out evaluation. Use a private temporary directory owned by evaluation.py's work directory.

benchmarks/evaluation.py:57 and benchmarks/scientific_cases.py:49 call communicate() without a timeout after the group kill; a descendant that left the group and still holds the pipe keeps evaluate() from returning.

benchmarks/evaluation.py:52 does not validate the marker payload: invalid JSON or a non-object raises out of evaluate() and the evaluation is never logged; Infinity and booleans pass the score test at 62 and json.dumps then writes non-standard JSON to the log.

benchmarks/evaluation.py:28-30 enforces the documented single CPU core only through advisory environment variables; nothing pins affinity or limits process count, so a program can start several worker processes.

benchmarks/problems/kissing_number_11/evaluator.py:46 and 53-55 validate the packing with assert statements, which are removed when the evaluating interpreter runs with PYTHONOPTIMIZE or -O; the environment is inherited unchanged from the operator's shell.

benchmarks/problems/circle_packing_26/evaluator.py:20 reads the score scale from the ambient variable CIRCLE_PACKING_TARGET_VALUE, which evaluation.py:46 passes through; a stray value in the operator's shell silently rescales every score of that problem.

benchmarks/evaluation.py:46 places the evaluator in its own session without installing a termination handler, so in-flight evaluations are not stopped when the framework receives the end-of-budget SIGTERM (baselines/run_baseline.sh:54) and then run with no time limit.
